science.fieldQuestion: Is the Skinner Ridge block part of the lower Rockytop bedrock beside it, or a float block that came down from upper Rockytop?
science.decidingObservation: Contact observation decides the question. Facies comparison is supporting evidence.
science.inPlaceHypothesis: Initial mission report: in-place bedrock based on bedding parallel to Rockytop.
science.floatHypothesis: Williams et al. (2026): displaced float block from Upper Rockytop based on alternating protruding/recessive layering.
science.unresolvedGuidance: If regolith talus or shadows obscure the contact, designate strictly as unresolved — do not guess from parallel bedding.
science.wildcatTask: Record whether calcium-sulfate veins cut across depositional bedding to test for post-depositional alteration.
science.skinnerTask: Inspect contact continuity where the block meets adjacent bedrock. Document bedding orientation, thickness, and grain size.

caution.slopeThresholdsDescription: Along-route grade spikes from 15° at 5 m baseline up to 21–22° at 2 m sampling.
caution.dtmDiscordance: DTM model discordance on 5.2 m connector (~7° primary vs ~22° fallback)
caution.obstacleDescription: Large boulders at Betty's Rock, steep scarp talus, and eastern crack/overhang at Skinner Ridge.
caution.dataGapsDescription: Segments lacking valid terrain elevation coverage.
caution.turnaroundDescription: Farthest point from start and commitment to return leg before consumables deplete.
caution.clearanceRequired: Option cleared only after every caution zone has been reviewed.
caution.noClearance: Not recommended: unresolved caution zones or hazards along route.

weather.archivalNote: Archival MEDA weather in Jezero Crater (sols 490–516). Historical record, not a forecast.
weather.radDisclaimer: RAD measurements acquired at Gale Crater (~4.5° S), serving as contextual planetary baseline, not a localized Jezero forecast.
